slides.texte_overlay:
How to be more present
with the people you love
Leave your phone in another room during meals. Dinner becomes a real conversation instead of three people scrolling at the same table.
Ask better questions than "How was your day?" Try "What made you laugh today?" or "What's been on your mind?" Specific questions open real conversations.
Put tasks on hold when someone talks to you. Turn away from the laptop, look at them, listen. Ten seconds of full attention says more than an hour half there.
Plan time together that isn't on screens. A walk, a board game, cooking together. Shared activities create memories that a film night rarely does.
Before: always in my head, never really there. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, a calmer mind and real stories to share at dinner.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: always in my head, never really there. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. A calmer mind and stories to share at dinner.

slides.texte_overlay: Notice the small moments. Your partner's laugh, your dad's old jokes, your friend's new haircut. Being present means paying attention to the little things.
Say what you appreciate out loud. "I really love these Sunday breakfasts with you." People feel closest to you when they know they matter.
